title: With wisdom
hookLine: invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good counsel, and argue in the best way (16:125)

cards: Somewhere right now a comment thread about religion has gone on for two hundred replies. Nobody in it has changed their mind. Everyone in it has gotten a little meaner.
Near the end of An-Nahl there's a verse about exactly this: how to talk about faith with people who don't share yours, or don't share your reading of it. It doesn't tell anyone to stay quiet.
It tells them how to speak, and names three tools.

teach.b: Pickthall's translation of 16:125: "Call unto the way of thy Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation, and reason with them in the better way." Tool one: hikmah, wisdom.
The root h-k-m has to do with holding something firm and judging well; the classical dictionaries list, from the same root, hakamah, the part of a horse's bridle that steers and restrains.
Wisdom, in that picture, is knowing when to pull back: the right thing at the right time to the right person, or nothing yet.

teach.h: GOOD COUNSEL, FROM SOMEONE WHO CARES.
teach.b: Tool two: al-maw'izah al-hasanah, good counsel, the kind that comes from someone who obviously cares about you. Tool three is the surprising one. Jadil: argue, debate.

teach.h: ARGUE, BUT IN THE BEST WAY.
teach.b: It says argue billati hiya ahsan, in the way that is best. Ahsan shares a root with ihsan from yesterday: excellence, doing something beautifully. So even a disagreement is supposed to be done well.

teach.h: HE KNOWS BEST; THE RESULT ISN'T YOURS.
teach.b: Then the verse ends with a sentence that lowers the temperature of every argument: your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best who is guided.
In the verse's terms, the speaker answers for the manner; the outcome is God's.

teach.h: REASON WITH THEM IN THE BETTER WAY.
teach.b: Another verse, 29:46, makes the same point about the People of the Book: don't argue with them except in the best way. This week's verses were gifts: countless favors, milk from between, the bee, justice and excellence.
Today the gifts turn into a way of talking: wise, kind, and, when it comes to arguing, beautiful.

how: Muslim teachers cite 16:125 as the guiding verse for da'wah, inviting others to Islam, and for interfaith conversation; many emphasize gentle speech and leaving guidance to God.

o: secret knowledge kept for a chosen few only
wisdom: knowing when to speak, steer or hold back
winning a debate with the sharpest arguments

games.q: the three tools of 16:125 — tap the pairs.
p: good counsel from someone who cares
argue in the way that is best
the best way with the People of the Book

s: it allows argument, but only in the way that is best.
ahsan, best, shares a root with ihsan, excellence
the same root, h-s-n: even a debate is meant to be done beautifully.
the verse says winning the argument is your job
it ends: your Lord knows best who strays and who is guided.

games.q: a friend mocks your faith in front of others, and you know you could win the argument. 16:125 has three tools. which comes first in the verse?
games.why: wisdom comes first, then good counsel, then argument in the best way. and the verse ends by leaving the outcome to God.

practice: Bring to mind a disagreement you're in right now, about faith, politics, or whose turn it is to do the dishes, and picture the other person's face.

Slowly find the strongest version of their point, the one they'd be glad to hear you say, then picture saying your own view in a way they could hear without bracing. Don't plan to win; plan to speak well.

wordCard.voice: Hikmah. Wisdom, from a root about holding firm and judging well: the first tool for speaking about faith, before counsel and before argument. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: wisdom, from the root h-k-m, to hold firm and to judge.

carryVoice: Your line: argue in the best way. The outcome isn't yours to hold. Day four hundred fifty-five, and a week complete.

sources.q: Call unto the way of thy Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation, and reason with them in the better way.
